system.name: SchemaNet (schema inference)
system.one_liner: An image classifier that predicts by matching the instance's graph of visual ingredients to a learned graph for each category.

content.variant_note: one elephant photo followed from coloured patches to two weighted graphs, a matcher and a summed class score
content.argues: A class score can be read as the sum of evidence from matched local structures of the image's ingredient graph and the category graph, so the prediction is explainable.
content.subject: One elephant image: ingredient overlay, instance and category IR-Graphs, matched local structures of #198 and #150, and the score 21.25.

encoding.color_means: One colour per ingredient: orange #198, purple #150, red #133, green #46, blue #25, grey for the others. The colour marks its cells on the photo, its index in the table header, its vertices in both graphs, the local-structure title and the arrows and terms of the score.
encoding.line_style_means: thin grey lines = graph edges carrying weights; small black arrows inside ovals = neighbours feeding the centre vertex; long orange and purple arrows = evidence passed to the score
encoding.shape_means: circle = a vertex (ingredient); oval = a local structure; rounded box = a graph; big pale-green block arrow = the matcher
encoding.marker_means: #n is an ingredient index; numbers on vertices and edges are weights; 18.60 + 2.65 = 21.25 is the class score
encoding.emphasis: Only #198 and #150 are coloured thick and circled while the rest are grey, so the two matched structures stand out; the score line closes the figure.

new_tags.name: categorical-patch-overlay
new_tags.what: translucent colour-coded cells over a photo's patch grid, one colour per discrete visual word, reused as the node colours of the graphs

lessons.what_to_learn: Fix one colour per discrete concept and carry it from the image overlay through the table of examples and the graph vertices to the terms of the final score, so a prediction can be traced to its evidence. Show the matcher as a big labelled arrow between graph boxes and enlarge the matched local structures in ovals.
lessons.suits: Interpretable or prototype-matching models that predict by comparing an instance structure with class structures, where which parts matched and with what weight is the story.

evidence: the desired outputs from schema inference contribute only from the relationship of visual words, as shown in Figure 1.
The final prediction is defined as the sum of all evidence.

summary: SchemaNet classifies by matching graphs instead of using deep features: an image is split into feature ingredients (visual words) that form an instance ingredient-relation graph, which is matched against each category's learned graph. Figure 1 walks one elephant image through this. At left, a photo with a colour-coded patch overlay and a table of patch thumbnails show the ingredients. In the middle sit an Instance IR-Graph and a Category IR-Graph with coloured, weighted vertices. A pale green Matcher arrow leads to ovals around the local structures of #198 and #150 in each graph, whose evidence 18.60 and 2.65 sums to the class score 21.25.
summary_zh: SchemaNet 用图匹配代替深层特征分类：图像拆成成分，组成实例图，再与类别想象图匹配。图 1 以大象图为例：左侧着色补丁与成分示例，中间为加权图，右侧经 Matcher 对 #198、#150 的局部结构求和，得分 21.25。
notes: Prior labels kept (worked-walkthrough, stage-pipeline). Panels are three column groups; only the left strip is ruled off by a line, the two graph boxes are framed and titled. The figure does not say what the numbers on vertices and edges measure. The digest counts 37 placed bitmaps: the photo with overlay (72 pt), the small photo (25 pt) and 35 patch thumbnails (9 pt).
